What makes Ankylosaurus so amazing?

Covered head to toe in hard armor, Ankylosaurus is a herbivore dinosaur like a living tank. Even predators couldn't mess with it easily.

content.text:
Nature and science facts about Ankylosaurus

Ankylosaurus lived in North America about 66 million years ago and was 6-11m long. The armor plates (bone within the skin) covering its back were so extensive that even its eyelids were covered in bone. But its belly had no armor plates, so when an enemy appeared, it pressed its belly flat to the ground to hide its weak spot. It fought off predators with the hard club (hammer) at the end of its tail.

Points worth exploring together

Point out things like the back armor (bone plates), the tail club (its weapon), the weak spot (belly), and the defensive pose. Talking about "Why did it press its belly to the ground?" together is a great way to spark curiosity.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. How did Ankylosaurus protect itself?
A. It fought back with its full-body bony armor and tail club, and hid its weak belly by pressing it to the ground.

Q. Where was its weak spot?
A. Its belly. Since it had no armor plates there, it pressed its belly flat to the ground to hide it when an enemy appeared.

Q. How can we enjoy it at home?
A. Comparing its armor with a turtle or armadillo, and puzzling out "How did it protect its belly?" are great.
